knowledgeArticles.title: SOP: Resolve PostgreSQL Primary Node Replication Lag on postgres-prod-01 via WAL Sender Bottleneck and Network Buffer Tuning
knowledgeArticles.summary: Replication lag on postgres-prod-01 is caused by the primary's WAL sender process stalling due to insufficient `wal_sender_timeout` and default TCP send buffer sizes, causing the standby to fall behind during sustained write bursts. The fix requires increasing socket buffer limits in the OS kernel and adjusting PostgreSQL `wal_sender_timeout` and `max_wal_senders` to prevent premature connection termination and backpressure.
symptoms: pg_stat_replication shows 'write_lag' and 'flush_lag' exceeding 30 seconds with 'state' stuck in 'streaming' but 'sync_priority' = 0
Primary logs show 'WARNING: replication slot "slot_standby_01" has grown to 12 GB' indicating WAL retention pressure
netstat -s output on primary shows 'TCP sockets finished time wait in fast timer' and 'send buffer errors' incrementing rapidly
pg_control_checkpoint shows 'checkpoint_sync_time' spiking > 500ms during peak write load, blocking WAL sender flush
knowledgeArticles.rootCause: Default Linux kernel net.core.wmem_max (212992 bytes) and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem limits restrict the PostgreSQL WAL sender's TCP send buffer, causing the primary to block on socket writes during high-throughput checkpoints. Combined with a default wal_sender_timeout of 60s, the sender cannot drain the WAL fast enough, forcing the standby to request retransmission and widening the replication lag gap.
resolutionSteps: ssh root@postgres-prod-01

ssh root@192.168.100.101 "sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=16777216 && sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=16777216 && sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_wmem='4096 87380 16777216' && sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_rmem='4096 87380 16777216'"

ssh root@192.168.100.101 "echo -e 'net.core.wmem_max=16777216
net.core.rmem_max=16777216
net.ipv4.tcp_wmem=4096 87380 16777216
net.ipv4.tcp_rmem=4096 87380 16777216' >> /etc/sysctl.d/99-postgres-tcp.conf && sysctl --system"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "psql -U postgres -c \"ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_sender_timeout = '5min'; ALTER SYSTEM SET max_wal_senders = 20; ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_keep_size = '4GB';\""
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "systemctl reload postgresql-15 && watch -n 2 'psql -U postgres -c \"SELECT client_addr, state, write_lag, flush_lag, replay_lag, sync_priority FROM pg_stat_replication;\"'"

User 'ananya' absent from /etc/passwd and /etc/group (wheel, secops) on Control Plane
Sudoers configuration missing entry for 'ananya' preventing privileged command execution
knowledgeArticles.rootCause: New hire onboarding requirement: OS user account 'ananya' does not exist on the Control Plane server. The account, SSH authorized keys, group memberships (wheel, secops), and sudoers policy must be created to grant authorized access and administrative privileges.
resolutionSteps: ssh root@192.168.100.101 "id -u ananya &>/dev/null || useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G wheel,secops -c \"Ananya Iyer, Cloud Security Analyst\" ananya"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "mkdir -p /home/ananya/.ssh && chmod 700 /home/ananya/.ssh && chown ananya:ananya /home/ananya/.ssh"

ssh root@192.168.100.101 "cat > /home/ananya/.ssh/authorized_keys << 'EOF'
<PASTE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_HERE>
EOF
chmod 600 /home/ananya/.ssh/authorized_keys && chown ananya:ananya /home/ananya/.ssh/authorized_keys"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "echo 'ananya ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/ananya-secops && chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/ananya-secops && visudo -c -f /etc/sudoers.d/ananya-secops"

knowledgeArticles.title: SOP: Deprovision OS User 'kavya' (UID 1004) and Archive Home Directory on Control Plane 192.168.100.101
knowledgeArticles.summary: This procedure archives the user's home directory, revokes sudo privileges, and removes the OS user account 'kavya' (UID 1004) from the control plane server 192.168.100.101. The process ensures no residual access or files remain while preserving a compressed backup of the user data for compliance.
symptoms: Alerts triggered for Delete User Account 'kavya' on Control Plane Server
System degradation reported.
knowledgeArticles.rootCause: The steps follow a safe deprovisioning sequence: first verify the target account, then create a timestamped compressed archive of the home directory for audit/recovery, remove the dedicated sudoers drop-in file to immediately revoke elevated privileges, and finally use 'userdel -r' to atomically remove the user account, home directory, and mail spool. Post-deletion checks confirm the account is fully removed from authentication databases and filesystem, eliminating any lingering access vectors. Archiving before deletion satisfies data retention requirements while the '-r' flag ensures cleanup of associated resources.
resolutionSteps: ssh root@192.168.100.101 "id kavya"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "tar -czf /root/kavya_home_archive_$(date +%F_%H-%M-%S).tar.gz -C /home kavya"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/kavya"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "userdel -r kavya"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "id kavya 2>/dev/null && echo 'User still exists' || echo 'User successfully deleted'"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "ls -ld /home/kavya 2>/dev/null && echo 'Home directory still exists' || echo 'Home directory removed'"
ssh root@192.168.100.101 "ls -l /etc/sudoers.d/ | grep -i kavya || echo 'No sudoers file for kavya'"
